newsitem.title: GERMANY: IG Metall hails Volkswagen jobs plan.
newsitem.headline: IG Metall hails Volkswagen jobs plan.

text.p: Germany's IG Metall trade union on Wednesday hailed an innovative early retirement scheme to be introduced at car-maker Volkswagen an "excellent and socially-acceptable pact between the generations".

Klaus Zwickel, chairman of the metal and engineering workers' union that is Germany's largest organised labour group, said the deal reached late on Tuesday would create more opportunities for young people to obtain work.

According to VW, the plan allows workers aged 55 to opt to receive 85 percent of their net pay for the next five years. In return for working regular hours for the first 30 months of that period, they will be able to enter retirement at 57-1/2.

VW said the plan, which calls for it to ensure that state pension benefits for participants are maintained at full levels, could affect about 10,000 people during the next five years. The cost to VW is put at 150,000 marks ($86,900) per worker.
A VW spokesman further said the early retirement programme will also help allow VW to keep up to 1,000 trainees per year.

Zwickel called on the Gesamtmetall metal and engineering employers federation to modify their stance on such retirement schemes in regional sector talks currently taking place near Stuttgart, home to Daimler-Benz AG.
Employer negotiators there have resisted agreeing to terms that would make such schemes components of legally-binding work contracts.
